entries.title: Calif’s kernel exploit moves toward a public release.
entries.dek: Anna Groza is aiming to publish an exploit and write-up. opa334 describes a path to broader Dopamine support on A12 and A13. The code and exact support matrix are still pending.
entries.scope: A12 / A13 integration discussed; final firmware scope pending
observed: Anna Groza (@pwnlambda) said on November 3 that she is aiming to release the iOS kernel read/write exploit and write-up within roughly a week.
opa334 separately said he expects to extend Dopamine to the exploit’s supported versions on A12/A13 using momentarius. He said A14 and newer still need an SPTM bypass.
entries.meaning: This is a concrete publication plan with a jailbreak maintainer’s explanation of where the result could fit. A kernel read/write primitive would offer substantially more capability than a crash reproducer. The practical effect still depends on the released implementation and its exact support.
limits: The announcement is a release target, not a published exploit or a fixed jailbreak release date.
The source, final device/build matrix, and independent reproduction remain pending in this review.
The announcement does not establish that the upcoming exploit is the public AppleAVE2 temporal-layer PoC. Shared research credit does not establish an identical bug or primitive.

entries.title: A Lockdown Mode demo continues through an iOS update.
entries.dek: Calif’s new video shows tweak behavior returning after an update and reboot, with iOS 27.2 displayed. Persistence and a fresh compromise of 27.2 remain separate claims.
entries.scope: Reported iPhone 18 Pro; update sequence ends with iOS 27.2 displayed
observed: Calif posted a three-minute video on November 3 captioned “Lockdown Mode helps, until it doesn’t.” The video shows tweak behavior, an update/reboot sequence, and the behavior returning afterward.
MacRumors reports the device as an iPhone 18 Pro and describes the initial delivery as a PDF accepted through AirDrop.
entries.meaning: Surviving an update can matter even when the original entry point has been patched. The observed sequence supports a persistence demonstration on the shown setup; it does not identify the mechanism that restores the behavior.
limits: The video does not establish a fresh compromise of a stock device already running iOS 27.2.
No public implementation, persistence mechanism, or complete support matrix was verified.
The public demo was reviewed through its visible sequence. It has not been independently reproduced here.
entries.update: Tweak behavior returns after an update and reboot.
entries.priorityNote: Tweak behavior returns after an update to 27.2. A fresh compromise of 27.2 is not established.

entries.title: Liter8 becomes a more useful iPhone 11 lab.
entries.dek: Version 0.2.3 adds persistent Wi-Fi credentials and SFTP. The preceding release added optional kernel-task access. The tethered boot and hardware limits still define the project.
entries.scope: Base iPhone 11 (n104ap); documented builds through iOS 27.2 24B119
observed: v0.2.3 adds SFTP/SCP in normal boot and Wi-Fi password persistence across reboots without SEP.
v0.2.2 added an optional tfp0 boot patch. Published run notes document kernel reads and writes to a scratch allocation on 27.2 build 24B119, including a repeat boot.
The current README labels the base iPhone 11 as tested. The 11 Pro and Pro Max profiles remain experimental despite the broader wording in the release notes.
entries.meaning: The published code and run notes make this useful as a specialized research environment. Kernel access comes from a patched boot workflow built on usbliter8; it does not demonstrate a new app-to-kernel exploit on a stock running system.
limits: Every boot requires the tethered Mac/DFU workflow. Setup includes an erase restore.
SEP, passcode, and cellular data remain documented limitations. Calls and SMS rely on Wi-Fi Calling in the described setup.
The published write test uses scratch kernel memory. It does not establish writes to SPTM-protected memory.
Source and supplied run notes were reviewed; this setup has not been independently run here.

entries.title: A Canon RAW decoder walks backward out of its pixel buffer.
entries.dek: Project Zero’s report connects a signed geometry-check failure to a negative row step, with a crafted image and debugger evidence. The iOS 27 branch is already fixed.
observed: A malformed Canon sRAW image passes a signed arithmetic check. A separate unchecked component count produces a negative destination-row step.
The decoder then writes file-derived chroma samples backward below the pixel allocation. The report ties debugger observations and the crash address to the affected store.
The report supplies a crafted CR2 file and identifies the unmodified input as a working control.
entries.meaning: The published effect is a linear out-of-bounds write with file-influenced contents and an allocation-relative destination. The report assesses code-execution risk, but its published runtime result is a corruption reproduction, not a complete execution chain.
limits: Project Zero reports this fixed in macOS/iOS 27. Apple also lists the older-branch fix in iOS 26.7.2.
This does not supply an entry point for iOS 27.0.1 or 27.2.
The exact public reproduction is on a Mac. An equivalent iPhone delivery path and exploit chain have not been established by this review.

entries.title: A RAW-image correction loop runs beyond the allocation.
entries.dek: A Phase One decoder trusts a file-supplied correction length. A one-tag control and measured fault make the new Project Zero disclosure particularly useful to study.
observed: One segment of a flat-field correction loop lacks the row-width bound enforced on the neighboring segment.
The file influences both the loop extent and a per-row correction value. The effect is a constrained 16-bit read-modify-write that can extend beyond the decoded pixel allocation.
The report supplies a crashing IIQ image and a control differing in a single tag, alongside loop measurements and an allocation-boundary fault.
entries.meaning: The control isolates the missing bound more clearly than a standalone crash. This is credible public memory-corruption research. Freely chosen bytes, an arbitrary destination, and completed code execution are not established by the published reproduction.
limits: Apple lists the issue as fixed in iOS 26.7 and the iOS 27 branch.
Newly public technical detail does not make this a new unpatched iOS 27 entry point.
The supplied exact-build runtime evidence is on macOS; no independent iPhone reproduction was performed here.

entries.title: A link preview draws a later frame into an earlier frame’s buffer.
entries.dek: A detailed report connects received-link delivery to an out-of-bounds clear and draw. Neighboring-buffer writes add substance beyond the crash, with destination control still limited.
entries.scope: Detailed reproduction: macOS 26.7 (25G229); iPhone testing also reported
observed: LinkPresentation sizes a pixel buffer from the first image frame, then uses a later decoded frame’s dimensions for drawing.
The report documents an out-of-bounds clear, image-content writes, and changes to a neighboring live IOSurface. It also includes controls and a patched-build comparison.
Received-link testing reaches the affected transcoder after the recipient loads the Messages preview. Source was published October 29; the detailed report followed October 30.
entries.meaning: This is a strong public disclosure because it connects external delivery, a specific allocation mistake, and measured corruption. The input influences the overflow and contents; allocation layout determines the neighboring target.
limits: No arbitrary-address write or code-execution chain is published.
The reported Messages trigger requires loading the preview. It should not be presented as a demonstrated zero-click chain.
The most detailed build/process evidence is from macOS. Do not transfer its privileges or mitigation behavior to iPhone without matched evidence.
Apple lists fixes in iOS 26.7.2 and 27.2.

entries.title: The public AVE reproduction reaches a kernel fault.
entries.dek: Concrete encoding calls and a supplied panic support a crash reproduction. Useful kernel access and mitigation bypasses remain unproven.
observed: The app sets an oversized temporal-layer count through VideoToolbox and submits an encoding frame. The supplied panic identifies videocodecd and AppleAVE2.
The author describes the corruption as a fixed-offset constant fill, with no arbitrary kernel read/write. The README supplies a surviving input control and reports API rejection on iOS 27.2.
The author credits the original Calif/Chollima discovery and presents this project as a reproduction.
entries.meaning: The privileged fault makes this relevant to kernel research. A restricted write can be useful, but the public artifact does not identify a useful repeatable state change that execution survives.
limits: The faulting instruction’s offset, AppleAVE2 +0xDA78, locates the crash. It does not establish control of a write destination or identify the original overwritten object.
No memory-disclosure primitive, acquired kernel access, MIE bypass, or complete jailbreak is demonstrated.
The source and panic were inspected. Exact CVE attribution was not independently established by a driver binary comparison, and no on-device reproduction was performed here.

entries.title: A media service returns file access the client does not have.
entries.dek: The published app reads a daemon-opened descriptor while its direct open of the same path is denied. The demonstrated access is centered on the media library.
observed: The PoC asks mediaplaybackd to open a client-selected path and obtains a live file descriptor in the reply.
Source and supplied logs show reads through that descriptor, including SQLite content, alongside a denied direct-open control.
The tested accessible domain centers on the media library. Tested protected paths and writes remain denied.
entries.meaning: This is a completed, bounded access-control violation in the supplied evidence. The service acts with authority the client lacks, but receiving a descriptor does not grant general control of the service or change the client’s sandbox policy.
limits: The publication does not establish general filesystem access, service-process execution, or kernel access.
The path survey is bounded; it is not an exhaustive map of every readable or denied file.
The author reports an independent duplicate disclosure. Apple’s advisory credit is not independent validation of this repository’s reproduction.
The issue is reported fixed in iOS 26.7.2 and 27.2.

The separate CMap route in the same repository did not work through the tested vehicle.
entries.meaning: If independently reproduced, the reported value fingerprint would support more meaningful input influence than an unexplained crash. The published material is worth investigating, with its evidence limits kept visible.

Fixed-device behavior was assessed statically, not demonstrated in the supplied on-device run.
This is not evidence of two working exploits, code execution, or a jailbreak.
